ops.issue: 何時 must be read なんじ here: the sentence asks a clock time with に (en: 'What time...?', pt: 'A que horas...?'). いつ ('when') does not take に in this scheduling sense; なんじに is the standard reading.
Reading of token 何時 given as いつ; in this context (specific hour, followed by に, glossed 'what time / a que horas') the correct reading is なんじ.
Romaji encodes the same wrong reading いつ for 何時; should follow the correct reading なんじ (nanji).

The なんじ fix was applied to kana correctly (ちょうしょくわなんじに…) but the regenerated romaji is 'choushokuwan'anjiniitashimasuka.' — 'wan'anji' romanizes わんあんじ, not わ+なんじ. The apostrophe marks the wrong ん and inserts a phantom mora, so romaji no longer mirrors kana and the patch teaches a new wrong pronunciation while fixing the old one.

structure_explanation.en: The target here is いたします, the humble (謙譲語) form of the verb する ('to do'). The sentence follows the order topic + time adverb + verb: 朝食は (topic: 'breakfast'), 何時に (when: 'at what time'), いたします ('do', in humble register). The final か turns it all into a question. Since いたす lowers the one speaking/acting, the sentence treats the listener with respect, sounding polite and formal.

Como いたす rebaixa quem fala/age, a frase trata o interlocutor com respeito, soando educada e formal.

before.jp: 茶色がいいんですが。

structure_explanation.en: The sentence has the grammar focus on the construction ですが. Here 茶色がいい literally means 'brown is good/better', and the particle が marks 茶色 as the subject of what is 'いい' (preferable). The ん (= の) before です gives an explanatory tone ('it's that...'), and the final が is the adversative/attenuating が: instead of linking to a second clause, it leaves the speech open, softening the request ('I'd like the brown one, but... [is that okay?]'). It is a very common use, equivalent in English to leaving the sentence hanging to sound polite.

Aqui 茶色がいい significa literalmente 'o marrom é bom/melhor', e a partícula が marca 茶色 como o sujeito daquilo que é 'いい' (preferível). O ん (= の) antes de です dá um tom explicativo ('é que...'), e o が final é o が adversativo/atenuador: em vez de ligar a uma segunda oração, ele deixa a fala em aberto, suavizando o pedido ('eu queria o marrom, mas... [tudo bem?]'). É um uso muito comum em pt-BR equivalente a deixar a frase pendurada para soar educado.

structure_explanation.en: The sentence has a relative clause: 地下鉄へ行く ('that goes to the subway') directly modifies 道 (way), with no particle between the verb 行く and the noun. 道 is the object marked by を. The core is 教えて + いただけませんか, a very polite request: 〜ていただけませんか literally means 'couldn't I receive the favor of you ~?', that is, 'could you ~?'. The interrogative negative form (ませんか) softens and makes the request courteous.

O núcleo é 教えて + いただけませんか, um pedido bem polido: 〜ていただけませんか significa literalmente 'não poderia receber o favor de você ~?', isto é, 'você poderia ~?'. A forma negativa interrogativa (ませんか) suaviza e cortês o pedido.
